record.paper_title: Open problems on graphs arising from geometric topology
record.original_question: For finite graphs K, find structural descriptions of when K is basically embeddable into each of the product spaces R x S, T_3 x S, S x S, and X x Y where X and Y are graphs. Here S denotes the circle graph used in the obstruction list, T_3 denotes the 3-od graph used in products of stars, and a basic embedding into X x Y is the product-space analogue of a basic embedding into R^2: every continuous real-valued function on the embedded copy of K should decompose as the sum of one continuous function depending only on the X-coordinate and one depending only on the Y-coordinate.

artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return a definitive resolution of the structural characterizations of basic embeddability into ℝ×S, T_3×S, S×S, or general X×Y. Related work exists on basic embeddings of graphs into the plane and on embeddings of products of graphs into Euclidean spaces, but no source confirming a complete solution of these particular characterization problems was located.

status_evidence.title: Embedding products of graphs into Euclidean spaces
status_evidence.snippet: For any collection of graphs, the minimal dimension d is found such that the product of graphs is embeddable into R^d.
status_evidence.claim: Related work treats embeddings of graph products into Euclidean spaces, but does not address the basic-embedding characterizations sought here.
